questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mainly wanting to go to North America and Canada is much easier (and cheaper) in terms of visa. I wanted to explore more neuroscience and McGill was a great opportunity for this.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I signed up for the buddy program and outdoor frosh and both were great ways to meet new people and get a lot of advice and being shown around campus before the semester start. You also get a contact at the university and it's always worth just emailing and asking about anything you're unsure of.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introduction talk at first and above mentioned.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We were 3 people looking for at place together in different facebooks groups and got lucky - definitely worth trying. Residence is pretty nice but also quite expensive and has a mandatory meal plan. Look for places in Pleateau/Mile end area! Start looking early!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The city is pretty easy to get around but definitely look at commuting time. I had 40 minutes walk which was perfectly fine and for most of the time we used the Bixi bikes a lot but the metro is also great. So look for walking distance and metro lines.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's a really long process with lots of steps but it's so worth it! Once you get the spot at KU it's really easy to apply to McGill.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get a ton of emails and just have to go through them step by step. And there are steps on Minerva (their portal) to go through as well.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very much at first. Since people already studying at McGill gets to choose first. Be quick at first and try to register for the course you want right when it opens. Afterwards sign up for waiting lists - I got a spot of multiple courses this way. There is also a 2 week add/drop period at the beginning of the semester and I got exactly the classes I wanted at the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry too much if you don't get into the classes you wanted at first, you have plenty of time. There is also an app called seatalert to give you notifications when a spot becomes free for the classes without a waiting list.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Pretty similar to at home. But many more weekly assignments, quizzes and midterms.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Many classes consist of just lectures which is a bit boring this is however mainly for 300 level and below classes. 400 and 500 will be of in class teaching style. 300 and below has more of a midterm - final structure and 400 and above has more bigger assignments and much less memorization.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PHGY 314 - Integrative Neuroscience
COMP 204 - Computer Programming for Life Sciences
BIOL 414 - Invertebrate Brain Circuits and Behaviors
PSYC 311 - Human Cognition and the Brain

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Great combination of classes if you are interested in neuroscience. PHGY 314 and PSYC 311 have some overlap but not very much - it does help with learning the neuroanatomy though. Both are rather tough classes and mainly PHGY 314 is really interesting but also has soo much material. COMP 204 is great for python introduction. BIOL 414 is such a great class with really interesting material. You do need to know a little bit of coding before though, but it's really not much. I taught myself a bit of python for BIOL 414 which also made COMP 204 much easier so highly recommend doing that!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Data for your phone is much more expensive. Get a sim card with data in Denmark that you can use in Canada before going!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and clothing was a little more pricy than expected. I didn't have to buy any books which saved me a lot. Save up money before going since going on weekend trips is so worth it - but also a little expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many clubs at McGill. If you haven't found anything interesting before hand then go to the activities night and check out all the clubs. Also follow SSMU on instagram - they host a lot of stuff.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to outdoor frosh!! Great way of meeting other exchange students and the leaders will be same age as you and it's totally fine to talk to them as well since you might have some of the same classes! The lettuce club is legendary as well!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes! You can rent cars from enterprise through McGill to get a big discount. Go to other cities as well - Toronto and Niagara falls are great and you McGill has mustbus to get there for cheap!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. McGill is very international and it's easy to fit in. Some people might speak french to each other and you have to get used to that in general. Quebec is very french!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join everything to begin with. Everyone is looking for new friends at the beginning. A great start is going to outdoor frosh and joining camping which is more chill and more people. Go to club meetings and talk for people in class as well. Meetup with other danes on exchange as well.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't speak any french.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How international Montreal and McGill is.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go on outdoor frosh. 
Higher levels classes does not necessarily mean more work. 
Choose classes that sound interesting - if you have fun with your classes you will have much more energy for also doing other things.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't get too much into a mindset of what your exchange should be. There are so many opportunities and the most important thing is just to be open.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning a lot of neuroscience and meeting so many nice people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The application proces - it's soo long but once you go it's much easier! 
You have a lot of exams to balance out.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
